description: The review board is a plugin (off by default, needs the huddle) for mockups that go through rounds of review. A board is one folder in a git checkout: a sidecar file and one immutable page per revision, so the folder alone rebuilds the board. The read side is: the boards folder setting (it must be a real folder holding a .boards-root file, inside a git checkout, and never the app copy, an app bundle or the app state folder), the list of boards with whose turn each is in (your turn, with claude, undelivered), one board in full with the rounds you sent word for word, a rescan after a hand edit or a git pull, and two agent tools to read them. The board page shows a board read only: a title strip with whose turn it is, a history bar of revisions with the rounds you sent as diamonds between them, and the mockup itself in a locked-down frame (scripts run, but it has no network, storage or login, and it can only point at tagged parts of the page). You can step through revisions, switch between the real width and a fit-to-width view, and pop the page out into a tab of its own. Claude opens a board on your screen with task_manager_board_focus. Claude publishes boards and revisions: task_manager_board_create starts a board for a task and task_manager_board_revision_add adds each next revision (a page, a summary and the prompts to answer); every revision posts a card on the task and by default puts the task in review. A revision's files are never changed once written, and a failed write leaves the board as it was. A revision may instead own its controls (payload_mode): the page posts its state, the board header has a draft light, a save stepper, a note for the agent and send, there is no sidebar, the page's state autosaves as one overwriting draft, every send makes a numbered save and only nudges the session to review the payload, and a theme picker repaints just the page in another Carnivore theme. Closed reviews: a board whose task is done is closed (derived on read, never stored, so reopening the task reopens it), and each project's page on the projects page has a closed reviews group listing them, newest closed first, while the plugin is on. A revision may also name a questions layer (task_manager_board_create and task_manager_board_revision_add take layer): claude sends a list of questions instead of writing the controls, and the board draws them inside the frame, with no page needed. The fields are yes or no, pick one, pick several, on or off, a short text and a long text, and each question has a small note key. Questions sit right under the part of the page they ask about, the rest in one section at the end, or all in one panel at the edge of the frame (a bottom sheet on a phone). Your answers autosave, step through saves and send exactly like a payload page, and arrive as values and notes keyed by the question ids.
examples: Set the boards folder to the design/boards folder of a dedicated checkout and see the two converted flow boards listed.
Ask task_manager_board_get for the step 0 board with since_round 5 and get only the rounds sent after that.
Claude posts r1 and r2 of a bottom bar mockup on task 526 and the task shows a card for each, in review.
Open the step 0 board in the center screen, step back through its revisions on the history bar, and pop it out into its own tab.

Pick option B, tick padding ok and write a note in the prompts panel that folds down from the header at 412 px, press send, and see the round as a card on task 526; send it twice and it still lands once.

From the phone session: task_manager_scratch_post with name phone, html '

shots

' and two files; open the Scratch task's board and both images show.
Pick another theme in the header and only the page repaints.

Claude calls task_manager_board_attachment_add on the step 0 board with spec.pdf and notes.md; task 526 gets one info naming both files and goes to review, and the paperclip key on the board shows 2. Press it and open spec.pdf in a new tab.

Open the notes panel on a prompt board, write a few lines with a heading and a list, press ? to see the hints, switch to preview, reload the page and see the words still there, then press send and the panel comes back empty.

Tick task 526 done in the Task Manager, open project 18 on the projects page, and see its bottom bar board at the top of closed reviews; tap it and the board opens in the center screen. Reply on the task to reopen it and the row leaves the group.

Claude asks 'keep the rail?' (yes or no), 'density' (pick one) and 'why' (long text) in a layer with no page; you answer, add a note on the first, and Send; Claude reads {values: {...}, notes: {...}} on the round.

Claude posts 40 findings as a rows layer; each row shows what you had, what it is now and Claude's take (marked, not picked), you pick fine, push back or decide later on each, add a note on two, and Send; Claude reads values and notes keyed by row id.

Claude demos a layout live: you watch the page change on each call, say 'bookmark that' when you like one, and the draft is kept as a named revision that asks for your review; with inline_picks on, the prompts sit right under their rows on the page.
how_to: Turn the review board on from the plugins page (it needs the huddle) and set the task manager folder (the boardsRoot setting) to an absolute path. New boards, and the pastes and artifacts of every task, are saved under it in a folder per project, then per task.
Call task_manager_boards_list, optionally with task set to a huddle item id, then task_manager_board_get with the slug.
After a hand edit or a git pull, POST /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/rescan reads the folder again.

Claude starts a board with task_manager_board_create (name, title, task, summary, html or file_path, viewport, prompts) and adds revisions with task_manager_board_revision_add; set request_review to false to post the card without putting the task in review.

Claude opens a board on your screen with task_manager_board_focus (board, optional revision); or open the review tab from the open menu and pick a board. Use the arrows or the history bar to move between revisions, the fit icon to switch between real width and fit, and the pop-out icon for a tab of its own.

On a board that asks prompts, press the prompts key in the header (it shows how many are unanswered): a panel folds down under the header. Tap an option, tick a check, write a note or pin one to a part of the mockup, then press the send icon. The line under it names the task it went to. A diamond on the history bar opens the round as you sent it; if it says not delivered, press resend or link the board to another task with the link icon. The flip icon swaps the mockup between this revision and the one before.

The page shows a file by naming it files/<name>. The first post with a name files a Scratch task and makes the board; later posts add revisions. A script can POST the same as multipart to /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/scratch. Clear it for good with the trash key on the board's title strip.

A payload board: Claude publishes a revision with payload_mode true, a page with its own controls (a list with checkboxes, say) that posts its state to the board. The page's state is saved automatically as one draft that is overwritten in place (kept in the sidecar, written a moment after you stop and when you leave), and reopening the board loads it back. Send is your press only: it makes the next numbered save, records a round with the state, your note and what changed since your last send, and nudges the session to review the payload; it does not paste the payload.

The theme picker in the header lists the Carnivore themes; the first entry follows the app's theme. Choosing one repaints only the page frame (the app around it does not change) and is remembered on this device.

The files are saved on the board's task with one info naming them, and the task goes to review. A script can POST the same JSON to /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/boards/{slug}/attachments. A scratch board takes no attachments.

On the board page, the paperclip key in the header shows how many files are attached; press it for the list, newest first, with each file's size, date and revision, and keys to open it in a new tab or download it.

Press the note key in the board header to open the notes panel in the top right corner. Write markdown, switch to preview, and press ? for the list of what the preview understands. Drag the bottom left corner to resize it; the size is kept on this device. The words survive a reload: a prompt board keeps them in its draft, a payload board in this browser, until a send goes through. On a phone it opens as a sheet from the bottom.

With the review board on, open a project on the projects page: under its session groups a closed reviews group lists that project's boards whose task is done (ticked), newest closed first, each with its task, revision count and how long ago it closed. Unfold it, press show all for the rest, and tap a row or open to bring the board back up as a page row. Reopen the task and the board leaves the group. Agents ask task_manager_boards_list with state closed and project set to the project's id.

Claude calls task_manager_board_create or task_manager_board_revision_add with layer {kind: questions, v: 1, title, items: [...]} and no html. Answer in the frame; each question has a note key. Your answers autosave as the draft and Send hands them back to Claude as values and notes.

Claude runs a board live with task_manager_board_live_set (each call overwrites one working draft: no new revision, no card, the task stays where it is); say 'bookmark that' (task_manager_board_milestone_add) to freeze the draft as a named revision, and task_manager_board_live_stop ends the session. The board header shows a live mark, a bookmark key and an end key.
media_exempt: the board page's screenshots are made by the pre-version-bump recapture (scripts/feature_capture.py) against a leased test slot, never by hand; until then the page is described in words
name: Review board
summary: mockups under review as a folder of files in a git checkout: Claude publishes revisions, and you and Claude read them.
where: The review board plugin on the plugins page, with its boards folder setting.
The task_manager_boards_list, _get, _create and _revise MCP tools, while the plugin is on.
The review tab of the pop-out page (/static/popout.html?tab=reviewboard&board=<slug>), shown in the center screen from a page row in the browser list.
POST /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/boards/{slug}/open and the task_manager_board_focus MCP tool.

The prompts panel that folds down from the board header, and POST /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/boards/{slug}/rounds (also /draft, /rounds/{round}/resend and PATCH /task); no MCP tool sends a round. The payload autosave is PUT /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/boards/{slug}/payload-draft.
The paperclip key in the board header and its fold; GET and POST /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/boards/{slug}/attachments and the task_manager_board_attachment_add MCP tool.
The notes panel pinned top right of the board page, opened from the note key in the board header (the same markdown editor as the notepad widget, with its ? hints key).

The closed reviews group on a project's page (the projects page, one project open), after its session groups, while the plugin is on; GET /api/v1/cplugs/reviewboard/boards?state=closed&project=<id> and task_manager_boards_list with state and project.

A review board whose revision names a questions layer: the questions are drawn in the page frame (inline under their parts, or in a panel at the frame's edge). A rows layer draws a list of rows to review, each with its own picks and a note.

A live board in the review tab: a live state word, a draft mark at the end of the history track, and a live row with bookmark and end keys; its prompts can sit inline under their anchored rows. MCP: task_manager_board_live_set, _milestone_add and _live_stop; routes POST /boards/live, PUT /boards/{slug}/live, POST /boards/{slug}/live/milestone, /live/end and /live/send.
